references.text: God as the shepherd who seeks out what is lost: 'I will seek the lost, I will bring back the strayed' (Ezekiel 34:16). Jesus applies this image to himself as the Son of Man who came to 'seek and save what was lost'.
The Lord himself says he will seek his sheep and care for them, 'as a shepherd cares for his flock' (Ezekiel 34:11-12). Jesus fulfills this prophecy by seeking out Zacchaeus and others who were lost.

The Lord is like a shepherd who tends his flock, gathers the lambs in his arms, and carries them close to his heart (Isaiah 40:11). This care for the lost is reflected in Jesus' statement about his mission.
The Messiah is anointed to 'preach good news to the poor' and 'proclaim freedom for the captives' (Isaiah 61:1). Jesus' mission to seek and save the lost is a fulfillment of this messianic prophecy.

Jesus tells the parable of the lost sheep and says that 'the Son of Man came to save what was lost' (Matthew 18:11-14). This is a close parallel confirming that Jesus' mission was to seek and rescue the lost.
Jesus says, 'I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners' (Matthew 9:13). This statement aligns with the message in Luke 19:10 about Jesus' mission directed toward the lost.

The parable of the lost sheep illustrates the same point: the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to search for the one that has gone astray (Luke 15:4-7). Jesus uses this image to explain why he associates with sinners.

Jesus says, 'It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance' (Luke 5:31-32). The mission purpose of seeking the lost is also clear here.

'For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world might be saved through him' (John 3:17). The theme of salvation matches Luke 19:10, where the Son of Man came to save what was lost.

Jesus says, 'I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full. I am the good shepherd' (John 10:10-11). The theme of the shepherd and the theme of salvation are directly linked to the mission of the Son of Man in Luke 19:10.
Paul writes, 'Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners' (1 Timothy 1:15). This is a direct confirmation of Jesus' mission as expressed in Luke 19:10.

The context around Luke 19:10 shows that the people grumbled because Jesus went into the house of 'a sinful man', but Zacchaeus repented, and Jesus declared that salvation had come to his house (Luke 19:7-9). Jesus' words in verse 10 summarize his mission to exactly such people.
